nodes.label: app_users - portal staff identity table
ledger_entries - rental financial ledger
rentals - core rental agreement record
tenants - per-operator configuration root
customers - renter record
payments - money received against a rental
vehicles - fleet record
rag_documents - pgvector embedding store
rag_sync_queue - embedding refresh work queue
delivery_locations - priced delivery/collection points
pickup_locations - tenant pickup point catalogue
installment_plans - per-rental payment plan header
scheduled_installments - individual dated charges
installment_notifications - dunning send log
bonzah_insurance_policies - partner insurance policy store
chat_channels - one channel per tenant-customer pair
chat_channel_messages - human chat message log
customer_users - customer auth identity bridge
blocked_dates - vehicle availability blackouts
Single consolidated app_users SELECT policy (staff directory visibility)
Rationale: multiple overlapping SELECT policies caused unexpected behaviour, so they are collapsed into one
is_tenant_admin_for() SECURITY DEFINER escape from app_users self-referential RLS
Rationale: helper is SECURITY DEFINER so the policy can read app_users without re-entering its own RLS
Final app_users SELECT policy: self OR super admin OR same-tenant head_admin/admin
Rationale: a logged-in user may have a different tenant_id than the tenant they are viewing
Rollback: is_tenant_admin_for() dropped one migration after it was introduced
Ledger RLS must tolerate NULL tenant_id because refund entries are sometimes written without one
Split ledger tenant isolation into separate SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies, NULL allowed only on read
Second attempt: NULL tenant_id widened to write paths too, justified as legacy data
Third attempt: same predicates re-scoped explicitly TO authenticated, service_role assumed to bypass
Fourth attempt: fall back to rental ownership because get_user_tenant_id() may not return the expected value
user_can_access_rental() SECURITY DEFINER gate joining rentals to app_users
Tenant impersonation: policy reads user_metadata.impersonated_tenant_id out of the JWT as the effective tenant
Decision: RLS disabled outright on ledger_entries
Rationale: ledger is only reached via rental_id, rentals carry their own RLS, and the ledger policies broke tenant impersonation
Refund line categorisation: Tax, Service Fee and Security Deposit become postable ledger categories
Manual payment reversal/void capability
Documented payment status vocabulary: Applied=fully allocated, Credit=unallocated, Partial, Reversed=manually voided
Tenant-scoped RAG knowledge base over pgvector 1536-dim embeddings
Change-data-capture fan-out: six domain tables queue every row change for re-embedding
match_documents cosine-similarity retrieval, hard-filtered to one tenant_id
get_rag_metrics precomputes fleet/rental/payment counts so the chatbot can answer numeric questions without retrieval
Latent RLS defect: rag_documents and chat_messages policies compare app_users.id to auth.uid() instead of app_users.auth_user_id
queue_for_rag() re-declared SECURITY DEFINER with pinned search_path
Rationale: the RAG trigger ran as the caller, so any authenticated write to rentals/customers/vehicles failed the rag_sync_queue service-role-only policy
Live availability sync: blocked_dates published to supabase_realtime so booking sees portal blackouts instantly
Vehicle delivery and collection service with per-location fees
Unauthenticated read of active delivery locations, explicitly for the booking app which has no auth
Rentals snapshot the address and fee alongside the location FK so historical rentals survive location edits
Installment payment plans: split a rental balance into scheduled dated charges
Per-tenant installment eligibility thresholds held as installment_config JSONB (min days, max installments)
Stripe card-on-file: customer, setup intent and payment method ids persisted so later installments charge unattended
Plan generation: evenly divides the installable amount and emits weekly/monthly dated rows in one transaction
Cron-facing due query: only returns rows whose plan is active and already has a stored payment method
Settlement roll-up: marks the row paid, recounts the plan, advances next_due_date and auto-completes the plan
Dunning rule: an installment goes overdue only after 3 failures AND 3 days past due
Each scheduled installment carries payment_id and ledger_entry_id so settlement reconciles to money and ledger
Security trade-off: anon may INSERT and SELECT every installment plan and schedule with USING(true), to serve the unauthenticated booking flow
Batch overdue sweep re-implementing the 3-failure/3-day rule across all tenants
T-3-day reminder feed: one join assembling customer, vehicle and rental fields the notification template needs
Idempotent dunning: UNIQUE(installment_id, notification_type) plus upsert stops duplicate sends on cron re-runs
Trigger derives tenant_id for a notification by walking installment to plan, so callers never pass it
Gotcha: the three pg_cron jobs exist only as commented SQL and must be created by hand, so this file is not a map of live scheduling
Odometer tracking: reading captured at each key handover and mirrored onto the vehicle as current_mileage
Pickup locations: FOR ALL policy split per operation because the combined form did not admit INSERT
Decision: tenant scoping removed from pickup_locations RLS entirely - any authenticated user gets full access and the app is trusted to validate tenant
Bonzah insurance policies purchased inside the booking flow
Quote-to-policy state machine: quoted, payment_pending, active, cancelled, failed with separate quote/payment/policy ids
Rationale: anon may insert a policy because the row is created before payment, during the unauthenticated checkout
Rentals carry insurance_premium and a bonzah_policy_id back-reference, making insurance part of rental pricing
Human tenant-to-customer chat: one channel per tenant-customer pair
Dual-identity RLS: every chat policy exists twice, once resolving app_users (staff) and once customer_users (renters)
Polymorphic sender: sender_id means app_users.id or customers.id depending on sender_type, with no foreign key to enforce it
Denormalised per-participant unread_count, last_read_at and mute flags rather than counting messages on read
Stale rationale: service_role access is justified 'for Socket.IO server', a transport since replaced by Supabase Realtime
Naming collision: chat_messages is the AI/RAG transcript while chat_channel_messages is the human conversation
Decision: chat helper functions and last-message/unread triggers deleted in favour of direct queries in application code
Super admins granted cross-tenant read/write on all chat tables via is_super_admin() escape hatch
Chat presence: is_online and last_seen_at persisted per participant with partial indexes for online lookups

hyperedges.label: Six-migration ledger RLS escalation ending in RLS being switched off
Installment lifecycle: plan creation to due sweep to settlement, failure and overdue dunning
RAG indexing pipeline: domain-table triggers to sync queue to embeddings to tenant-scoped retrieval
